key_insight: A thermodynamically consistent phase-field model couples donor–acceptor phase separation, solvent evaporation, and fluid motion during organic solar-cell active-layer formation.
engineering_relevance: The model provides a mathematical foundation for studying how drying and flow shape organic photovoltaic active layers.
method: Couple incompressible Navier–Stokes, multispecies Cahn–Hilliard, and Allen–Cahn equations with cross-diffusion.
Use a specialized variational formulation for diffusion fluxes to handle degenerate mobility.
Prove global-in-time weak-solution existence without size constraints on the data.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports analytical guarantees of solution existence and total-energy dissipation, but no experimental validation or numerical benchmarks.
watch_item: Degenerate mobility complicates diffusion-flux formulation and requires care in numerical implementation.
paper_title: Modeling and analysis of a phase-field model for organic solar cells
